story.title: Every validator code can be looked up
story.source_text: When validate.py reports a code like BRF009 there is nowhere to look it up: 55 of the 153 codes the validator and batch.py can emit are documented in no reference file, so a maintainer or an implementer reading a finding has to open the validator source. Add `validate.py --codes` that lists every code with the phase it belongs to and what it means, generate references/codes.md from it, and make selftest's docs-consistency suite fail when a code can be emitted that codes.md does not list, so the index cannot rot. Maintainers only; nothing changes for someone running the validator today.
story.summary_human: A finding like BRF009 is currently a dead end unless you open validate.py: 55 of 153 codes are documented nowhere. This adds an explicit registry of every code with a one-line meaning, a `--codes` flag that prints it, a generated `references/codes.md`, and two selftest checks that fail the moment a code is emitted without an entry or the file goes stale. Two subtasks, one repo, half a day each.
story.technical_notes_human: Codes are string literals at the call site (`validate.py:158`, `batch.py:188`); none is built dynamically (ruled out). D1: an explicit per-module `CODES` dict beats regex-extracting message templates - the messages are %-format prose spread over lines, and only an explicit set lets selftest check both directions. D2: `codes.md` is committed and selftest asserts it equals `--codes --markdown`, so it is readable without running anything and cannot rot. D3: BAT codes get a `PHASE_OF` entry so they do not fall into '9 other'. `--codes` makes the bundle positional optional (`validate.py:1634`). The docs suite at `selftest.py:640` already checks docs -> code; S2 adds code -> docs. The manifest guessed `pytest tests/`; there is no tests/ - the test command is selftest.py.

intake.domain_rationale: Every fact needed is in two files and the selftest; it takes reading, not probing. Nothing here is knowable only by trying.

decisions.question: Where does the meaning of a code come from?

options.label: Regex-extract the message template from each rep.error/warn call
options.tradeoff: no new source of truth; templates are %-format prose over several lines and read badly; no way to detect a dead entry

options.label: An explicit CODES dict per module with a one-line meaning
options.tradeoff: one more thing to maintain; but a set both directions of the selftest can compare

decisions.chosen: An explicit CODES dict per module with a one-line meaning
decisions.rationale: A reader wants the condition, not the message; and the both-ways check in AC3 is only possible against an explicit set.

decisions.question: Is codes.md committed, or generated at test time?

options.label: Generated by selftest, never committed
options.tradeoff: cannot rot; but unreadable in the repo or an installed skill without running Python

options.label: Committed, with selftest asserting it equals the generator's output
options.tradeoff: one regeneration step per code change; readable everywhere

decisions.chosen: Committed, with selftest asserting it equals the generator's output
decisions.rationale: The skill is installed as plain files and read by agents that may not run scripts; a committed file is the only one they see.

decisions.question: Where do batch.py's BAT codes sit in the phase grouping?

options.label: Leave them; phase_of returns '9 other'
options.tradeoff: nothing to change; five codes land in a bucket named 'other'

options.label: Add BAT to PHASE_OF as its own group
options.tradeoff: one dict entry; the grouping in validate.py output changes for nobody, since batch codes never appear there

decisions.chosen: Add BAT to PHASE_OF as its own group
decisions.rationale: 'other' is where meaning goes to die; the group costs one line.

open_questions.text: Should references/codes.md also get a row in SKILL.md's reference table, or is the Scripts bullet enough?
open_questions.guess: Yes, one row: 'Any time validate.py names a code you do not know'. Left out of this story so the table edit is not made while the answer is open.

open_questions.text: Is the success signal 'zero undocumented codes, enforced by selftest' - or is a generated index without the gate enough?
open_questions.guess: Enforced. An index without the gate is the state we are in now, one release later.

open_questions.text: Severity column: is 'error | warn' acceptable for a code emitted at both severities (DOD001, BAS003), or should such codes be split?
open_questions.guess: Keep one code with 'error | warn'; splitting renames codes people may already cite.

conventions.rule: Every code is a string literal as the first argument of rep.error(...) / rep.warn(...).
batch.py reports through local error()/warn() closures, same literal-first shape.
Phase grouping is the PHASE_OF prefix map; phase_of() picks the longest matching prefix.
Scripts are stdlib-only, no network; selftest prints the assertion count rather than docs claiming one.
The docs suite already verifies docs -> code with a regex over references and config; extend it, do not add a second suite.

ruled_out.conclusion: A registry keyed by the literal is complete; do not add runtime discovery of codes.

glossary.means: The stable identifier of a finding, e.g. BRF009: a 3-6 letter prefix naming the family plus three digits. Cited in docs, comments and PRs, so it never changes meaning.
The explicit dict of every code a module can emit, with a one-line meaning (D1). New in this story.
selftest suite 16, 'docs consistency': paths, flags and codes cited in SKILL.md and references must exist.
